newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Northwest plan sees open power market by 1999.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Northwest plan sees open power market by 1999.

text.p: A committee will submit to the governors of Idaho, Oregon, Washington and Utah on Thursday plans for restructuring the region's electricity industry, a spokesman for the Northwest Power Planning Council said Tuesday.
The proposal includes introducing open access for retail buyers by July 1999, said spokesman John Harrison.
The review of the region's power system was launched by the governors in January, when a committee composed of utility representatives, policy makers and consumers was convened.

"The governors will use the plan to draft their own recommendations which will then be presented to (the Northwest's) congressional delegation," said Harrison. "We want to have an influence on expected federal and state legislation."

The review also calls for dividing Bonneville Power Administration, the federal agency which markets power produced at federal dams in the Northwest, into separate transmission and power marketing units.
The proposed plan argues for the Northwest to retain its "preference" status for sales of the federal power.
